title: Build slice 1 of native PR landing: owned-mode core, answering N1-N4
summary: Read as slice 1 of several: amend the design to answer review 3's N1-N4, and build a tested library module for owned mode (PR link store, push guard, merged-content check). No CLI command, no `gh` calls, and no stealth mode yet; those are later slices.

defaults_applied.how: Split into slices and build only owned-mode core logic plus the design answers.
The new module ships with passing tests, clippy clean.
The design is amended for N1-N4 before the code relies on it.
The push guard is enforced in code, not prose.
Host calls will use the existing `gh` client in a later slice; no new crate is needed now.
Docs and comments are written for an outside reader.

assumptions: The design is too big for one job, so this job is slice 1. Later slices are the `athena land --pr` command with `gh` calls, stealth mode, and the roadmap order change.
N2 is answered by keeping the PR number, host, repository and pushed head in the state directory in both modes. The repository's records schema does not change.

N1 is answered by comparing the merged commit's tree with the verified tree (the fingerprint). A mismatch leaves the job in a named 'merged-unverified' state. The user can re-verify that job on the new tip as a new job. The diff branch is dropped.

N3 and N4 are stated in the design text. The stealth body drops the job id and Athena vocabulary, the leak check covers the body, and stealth pushes a neutral branch name. For a multi-job squash in stealth mode, the earlier jobs get the per-job checks over the local store.
The first slice is pure library code with the git and host calls behind traits or fakes, so it can be tested without a network.
I read only the design, review 3, and the land.rs header. I did not read the existing record schema or the state-directory layout, so the module's exact home is a guess.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/native-pr-landing.md gains text for N1: the exact comparison (merged tree against the verified fingerprint), the named state of a merged-but-refused job, and how the user moves it out of that state.
The design states for N2 that the PR number, host, repository and pushed head live in the state directory in both modes. The status line no longer says 'Not yet re-reviewed' and cites review 3.

The design states for N3 what the stealth PR body keeps and drops, that the leak check covers the body, and that stealth pushes a neutral branch name. It also states how the push restriction to the job's own branch is checked.
The design states for N4 which per-job checks run over the local store when several jobs are squashed in stealth mode.

A new owned-mode module exists in athena-core. It stores and loads a PR link record (PR number, host, repository, head commit id, job id) under the job's state directory, outside the repository's records/.
The module has a push guard that refuses any branch other than the job's work branch and any non-fast-forward push. It has no force option.
The module has a merged-content check that returns a 'merged but not verified' result on a tree mismatch. The merge is found by the stored PR number and never by parsing trailers.

Run `cargo test`. Tests pass for the guard refusing a non-fast-forward and a wrong branch, for a lookup by PR number on a merged commit with a trailing Co-authored-by paragraph and no Athena trailer, and for the mismatch result on a disjoint-file case.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.

out_of_scope: The `athena land --pr` CLI command and any call to `gh`
Editing records/, athena.toml, defaults.toml, or CI workflows
departures: Higher than the reference: this job needs a design amendment plus a new module with tests in a large codebase I have not read in depth.
